items.text: Microsoft says it anticipates 2,000 jobs for the completed phase of its southeast Wisconsin datacenter development, with about 500 full-time employees and contractors hired for the first datacenter by the end of 2026.
items.source: Microsoft — Microsoft datacenters in Wisconsin fact sheet (Oct 2025)

items.text: Microsoft says construction of the new datacenters will require about 12.1 million work hours and more than 2,960 jobs at peak activity.
items.source: Microsoft — Microsoft datacenters in Wisconsin fact sheet (Oct 2025)

items.text: At the June 23, 2026 opening of the first Fairwater datacenter, Microsoft counted about 550 employees and vendors on site and expected about 800 when the second facility opens in 2028; wages and the share of Racine County hires were not disclosed.
items.source: Racine County Eye via Civic Media — Microsoft opens the Fairwater data center in Mount Pleasant (Jun 24, 2026)

items.text: Microsoft says it is partnering with We Energies on the energy infrastructure for the campus "while ensuring we pay our fair share and protect other ratepayers," and is adding carbon-free supply equal to its use, including a 250 MW solar project in Portage County.
items.source: Microsoft — Microsoft datacenters in Wisconsin fact sheet (Oct 2025)

items.text: In a preliminary April 24, 2026 decision (final order pending), the PSC of Wisconsin approved a modified We Energies Very Large Customer tariff (docket 6630-TE-113) that applies to loads of 100 MW or more, sets a 15-year minimum term, and requires these customers to pay 100% of the costs of generation built for them.
items.source: Public Service Commission of Wisconsin — PSC Overhauls We Energies' Data Center Tariff (Apr 24, 2026)

items.text: Microsoft says its Wisconsin facilities will mostly use closed-loop, zero-water direct-to-chip cooling, with a smaller share of servers on direct evaporative cooling used less than 5% of the year (above 85°F), and that it will buy water from the City of Racine.
items.source: Microsoft — Microsoft datacenters in Wisconsin fact sheet (Oct 2025)

items.text: Records released by Racine project peak use of 234,000 gallons a day (about 2.8 million gallons a year) in phase one and up to 702,000 gallons a day (about 8.4 million gallons a year) at full buildout, within Racine's 7-million-gallon-a-day Lake Michigan diversion approved in 2018 for Foxconn.
items.source: Wisconsin Public Radio — Microsoft data centers could use 8 million gallons of water each year (Sep 17, 2025)

items.text: Microsoft says it will use vegetative screening and building setbacks where possible, place downward-directed exterior lighting to limit light pollution, and have its contractors comply with local noise ordinances during construction.
items.source: Microsoft — Microsoft datacenters in Wisconsin fact sheet (Oct 2025)

items.text: Under its 2023 agreement with the village, Microsoft guarantees a minimum assessed value of $1.4 billion on its investments in TID 5 Areas II and III by Jan. 1, 2028, with no additional public financial incentives.
items.source: Wisconsin Public Radio via Urban Milwaukee — Mount Pleasant Deal With Microsoft Has No Public Subsidies (Nov 14, 2023)

items.text: Microsoft paid $3.8 million in property taxes to Mount Pleasant in 2025 on its 2024 tax bill, according to the village.
items.source: Racine County Eye via Civic Media — Microsoft opens the Fairwater data center in Mount Pleasant, corrected (Jun 24, 2026)

items.text: Microsoft's proposed 15-building expansion sits in tax increment districts expected to generate about $45 million (Durand Avenue) and $30 million (International Drive) a year for the village once district debts are paid.
items.source: Wisconsin Public Radio via Urban Milwaukee — Microsoft wants to build 15 more data centers in Mount Pleasant (Jan 20, 2026)

items.text: New York State says the Micron project will create 9,000 new jobs on site and up to 50,000 permanent jobs in the region over 30 years.
items.source: Office of the Governor of New York — Governor Hochul announces over $43 million in community investment funding (Mar 27, 2026)

items.text: The $500 million Green CHIPS Community Investment Fund is funded and distributed over 20 years, with $250 million from Micron and $100 million from New York State, for workforce development, education, community investments and housing.
items.source: Empire State Development — Green CHIPS Community Investment Fund (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: The first awards from the fund totaled over $43 million: nearly $35 million from Micron, including $30 million to the Housing CNY Fund, and $8.5 million from the state.
items.source: Office of the Governor of New York — Governor Hochul announces over $43 million in community investment funding (Mar 27, 2026)

items.text: Micron estimated it would need up to 48 million gallons of water a day at full buildout, mostly from Lake Ontario via the Onondaga County Water Authority, and says it aims for 100% water conservation through recycling and restoration.
items.source: WRVO — Micron estimates needing up to 48 million gallons of water a day (Aug 2, 2023)

items.text: Micron says it aims for 100% renewable electricity at the Clay site.
items.source: WRVO — Micron estimates needing up to 48 million gallons of water a day (Aug 2, 2023)

items.text: National Grid will expand its White Pine substation by about seven acres and run eight 345 kV lines, two per fab, under Caughdenoy Road; it has not disclosed the cost.
items.source: CNY Central — National Grid ramps up power and gas links as Micron fabs rise in Clay (Oct 5, 2026)

items.text: The Onondaga County IDA approved a 49-year PILOT under which Micron pays $84.5 million, against $283.9 million in property tax exemptions, and authorized the lease or sale of 820 acres of White Pine Commerce Park for $30 million.
items.source: Spectrum News — Onondaga County IDA votes on Micron land transfer, tax breaks (Nov 18, 2025)

items.text: Under the AEP Ohio data center tariff adopted by PUCO on July 9, 2025, new loads of 25 MW or more pay for at least 85% of their highest billing demand, for a ramp period of up to four years plus eight years, with an exit fee of 36 months of minimum charges.
items.source: AEP Ohio — Data Center Tariff (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: The city says its data centers do not use large amounts of water daily and that it has not needed additional water capacity because of them.
items.source: City of New Albany — New Albany Data Centers (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: The city reports four noise complaints from an operational data center in 15+ years, plus September 2025 complaints about exhaust fans at Google's campus, with a permanent fix scheduled to start installation in June 2026.
items.source: City of New Albany — New Albany Data Centers (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: The city says data centers paid $10 million in community development charges for tax year 2024, abatements usually cover the first 10 or 15 operating years, and abated companies must make minimum annual payments.
items.source: City of New Albany — City Finances (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: The Municipality of Kincardine says Bruce Power employs more than 4,200 people and that its Major Component Replacement project, begun in 2016, creates 22,000 jobs and adds $4 billion a year to Ontario's economy through 2033.
items.source: Municipality of Kincardine — Bruce Power (accessed Oct 27, 2026)

items.text: For its proposed Bruce C expansion of up to 4,800 MW of new nuclear generation, Bruce Power signed a four-year, $2.2 million agreement funding Kincardine's studies of water, waste, emergency response, transit and recreation needs.
items.source: Sarnia News Today — Kincardine and Bruce Power partner on infrastructure and readiness agreement (May 15, 2026)

items.text: TerraPower says it is mobilizing about 1,600 construction workers for the Natrium plant and expects about 250 full-time staff once it operates.
items.source: TerraPower — TerraPower Commences Construction on America's First Utility-Scale Advanced Nuclear Power Plant (Apr 23, 2026)

items.text: Lead contractor Bechtel left the project in September 2026, leaving Kemmerer's plans to house up to 1,600 workers in limbo; Bechtel said it does not expect the schedule to change, and completion is still expected around 2030.
items.source: Cowboy State Daily — Kemmerer plans for 1,600 nuclear plant workers in limbo after contractor backs out (Oct 13, 2026)

items.text: TerraPower says the plant pairs a 345 MW sodium-cooled fast reactor with molten-salt storage that can raise output to 500 MW.
items.source: TerraPower — TerraPower Commences Construction on America's First Utility-Scale Advanced Nuclear Power Plant (Apr 23, 2026)

items.text: In exchange for an 85% property tax abatement through Abilene's economic development corporation, Crusoe committed to 357 new full-time jobs and up to $3.5 billion in spending.
items.source: Business Insider via AOL — Oracle got big tax breaks (Jul 17, 2025)

items.text: About 9,000 craft workers were on site daily in March 2026, with construction of the eight buildings expected to run through the first quarter of 2027.
items.source: KTXS — Construction on Stargate One data center campus set to run through early 2027 (Mar 5, 2026)

items.text: Crusoe says the campus connects directly to the ERCOT grid, mainly using wind power, with GE Vernova gas turbines as backup power in place of diesel generators.
items.source: Crusoe — An inside look at the Abilene AI data center (Aug 5, 2025)

items.text: Crusoe says its closed-loop, non-evaporative cooling needs an initial fill of about 1 million gallons of municipal water per building, across eight buildings, plus about 50,000 gallons per building per year.
items.source: Crusoe — An inside look at the Abilene AI data center (Aug 5, 2025)

items.text: Crusoe says that once fully operational the campus will provide up to 32% of the City of Abilene's and up to 25% of Taylor County's FY 2025 budgeted property tax revenue.
items.source: Crusoe — An inside look at the Abilene AI data center (Aug 5, 2025)
